**Sikhae (시계) – Korean Traditional Rice Cake** Sikhae is a simple, comforting dish made from steamed rice flour (also called “sikhae” or “rice cake”) mixed with a savory broth. It’s often served as a side dish or snack, especially during festivals or family gatherings. Below is a straightforward recipe you can try at home. --- ### Ingredients | Item | Quantity | Notes | |------|----------|-------| | **Rice flour (sikhae)** | 1 cup (120 g) | Use fine‑ground rice flour; if unavailable, you can use glutinous rice flour (sweet rice flour) for a chewier texture. | | **Water** | 2 cups (480 ml) | Adjust slightly for desired consistency. | | **Salt** | ½ tsp (2 g) | For seasoning the dough. | | **Vegetable oil** | 1 tbsp (15 ml) | For greasing the steamer or pan. | | **Optional flavorings** | | • Soy sauce (1–2 tsp)
• Sesame oil (½ tsp)
• Garlic powder or minced garlic (½ tsp)
• Green onions, sliced (for garnish) | --- ### Equipment - Steamer or a pot with a steaming rack (or a large saucepan with a lid). - Mixing bowl. - Whisk or spoon. - Heat‑resistant container or small steamer basket. --- ### Instructions #### 1. Prepare the Steamer 1. Fill the steamer pot with water, ensuring it doesn’t touch the bottom of the steamer basket. 2. Bring the water to a gentle boil. 3. Lightly grease the steamer basket or the heat‑resistant container with vegetable oil to prevent sticking. #### 2. Make the Rice Flour Dough 1. In a mixing bowl, combine the rice flour and salt. 2. Gradually add the water while whisking continuously to avoid lumps. 3. Stir until you get a smooth, thick batter. - If the batter is too thick, add a little more water (a tablespoon at a time). - If it’s too thin, add a pinch more rice flour. #### 3. Steam the Dough 1. Pour the batter into the greased steamer basket or container. 2. Cover with a lid and steam over medium heat for **20–25 minutes**. - Check after 15 minutes: the dough should start to firm up but still be slightly translucent. - If you’re using a pot, keep the lid on and reduce the heat to low to avoid boiling over. #### 4. Finish and Serve 1. Once steamed, remove the sikhae from the steamer. 2. Let it cool slightly, then cut into bite‑size pieces or serve whole. 3. Optional: Drizzle a little soy sauce or sesame oil over the top, sprinkle with green onions, or toss with a pinch of garlic powder for extra flavor. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Texture**: For a softer, more delicate texture, use regular rice flour. For a chewier, stickier texture, use glutinous rice flour. - **Flavor Add‑Ins**: Mix in finely chopped kimchi, diced tofu, or shredded carrots into the batter before steaming for a more colorful, nutritious version. - **Serving Ideas**: - **As a side dish**: Serve alongside kimchi, pickled vegetables, or a light soup. - **As a snack**: Dip in a sweet soy sauce or a spicy gochujang sauce. - **With tea**: Pair with hot tea for a comforting beverage. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! If you’d like a more elaborate recipe or variations, let me know.
